Run started and planned. Here's the design I derived from the code, and the execution plan.

## Sort modes I'd ship (per column setting)

| Value | Order |
|---|---|
| `unread` ✅ default | tasks with unread messages first (newest first), then the rest by `updated_at` desc |
| `last_changed` | `updated_at` desc |
| `manual` | `sort_index` written by drag & drop, then `updated_at` |
| `priority` | high → medium → low, then `last_changed` |
| `due_date` | earliest due first, tasks without a due date last (overdue floats up naturally) |
| `created` | newest created first |
| `cost` | highest `cost` (cxjcoins) first |
| `name` | A→Z |
| `status` | canonical status order (`todo → doing → onhold → done → rejected`) — useful for "what's next" reading of a lane |

`priority` + `due_date` are the two that actually change how you *manage* a board (the kanban view currently ignores priority entirely); `cost` matters because it's a budget envelope. `sort_dir` is carried as an optional field so any mode can be inverted later without a new setting.

## What the code says (verified, not assumed)

- **Persistence seam**: `KanbanStore._normalize_columns` (`api/codx/junior/kanban/store.py` ~517) is the only path into `board.json` — it keeps `{id, title, color, folder, order, project_id, profiles}` and *silently drops* everything else. So the new `sort` must be added there with the same "explicit wins, omitted inherits" rule already used for `project_id`/`profiles`, otherwise any partial writer (an agent `create_column`, an old client) wipes it.
- **Sorting today is 100% client-side**: `buildViewColumns` (`client/src/store/kanban.js` ~470) maps `Object.values($storex.chats.chats)` and sorts inline (~497); `sprintColumns` does the same via `sortColumnTasks`. That's exactly the "thousands of chats" cost you want gone.
- **Unread primitive already exists but only in the browser**: `Message.read_by` + `POST /api/chats/markMessageAsSeen`. Computing it per board request would mean opening every message of every chat, so the plan denormalises `unread_counts` on `Chat`, maintained by `ChatManager` and the mark-as-seen path, with a `read_by` fallback for old chats.
- **`unread` as default is not free**: existing `board.json` columns have no setting, so the store defaults them on read — no migration needed.

## Plan (4 steps, sequential because each builds on the last)

1. `column-sort-storage` — `sort` (+ optional `sort_dir`) persisted in the store, constants in `kanban/model.py`, pytest for round-trip / default / unknown value / title inheritance.
2. `server-board-query` — `POST /api/kanban/chats/query`: server-side grouping, sorting, search, filters, per-column pagination and **dataset-wide** `total` / `unread_total` / `cost_total`; lightweight `ChatSummary` reader in `ChatManager` (no message bodies), denormalised unread counters.
3. `client-server-board` — board renders from that endpoint (no full chat map, no client sort/metrics), a `Sort` select in the column settings persisted through `saveBoard`, per-column "load more", and batched `sort_index` writes for `manual` drops only.
4. `docs-verification` — update `TASKS_BOARDS_SPRINTS.md` (§4.1, §5.4, new sort section, §9 read models, §13) + a `docs/features/` page, with a reviewer walking the acceptance list.

The background worker is already picking up step 1; the next round returns the results and I'll verify them against the acceptance criteria before closing the run.

is sound and needs no redesign.
